A quick thank-you — and a favor

Your story helps the next person get started.

I'm Andre Liu Orozco — most clients call me Coach Andre. After 15+ years coaching in San Francisco — small-group training, CrossFit, Olympic lifting, and working with clients through injuries, life changes, and every starting point in between — I'm starting a new chapter in Reno.

If we trained together, would you share what changed for you? 60–90 seconds is perfect. Record it, write it, add a photo if you have one — whatever's easiest.

Your status before training with Andre

Pain, injury, low energy, nervous about lifting — whatever was true for you.

Already diagnosed by your doctor? Say what your doctor said — and what your training looked like after.

Start with: “Before I started, I was…”
02

What's different now?

Strength, movement, confidence, daily life — carrying groceries, deadlifting again, keeping up with kids.

Start with: “Now I can…”
💡 Keep it specific

“I couldn't get off the floor without help, now I deadlift 135” lands harder than “great trainer!”

🎧 Quiet + close

Quiet room, phone an arm's length away. A stumble is fine — authentic beats polished.

⏱ Short is generous

60–90 seconds covering both questions. Writing instead? 3–5 sentences total.

Can this be shared?

Nothing is posted automatically. You can ask for edits or removal anytime.

One request: your own health situation is yours to share — mention it if you'd like. Just credit any diagnosis to the doctor who made it, not to your coach. Andre trains people who've been diagnosed; he doesn't diagnose.

Photo — if you have one 📸

Optional. A training photo beats a headshot.

What works best

  • You in motion — lifting, a class, mid-set. Not a posed headshot.
  • You and Andre, or you and your training group, if you have one.
  • Real over perfect — a phone photo is fine. Blurry is better than nothing.
  • No photo? Skip it. Audio or text on its own is plenty.
